rationale: The assistant recognised the electrical hazard straight away and told the customer not to touch the plug, socket or extension lead. It correctly worked out that washing-up liquid was the likely cause of the foam, and it recommended no part. However, it gave little practical help once the customer said they could not find the fuse box. It never asked whether they were standing in water or dry, never suggested contacting the landlord, and never said to call 999 if there was sparking or a fire. It also told them 'only the electricity emergency service can safely resolve' the hazard, which overstates what that service does for a fault inside a home. The same fuse-box advice and the detergent point were repeated across turns.
